text: The rating column records satisfaction from 1 (lowest) to 5 (highest). A blank rating means no response. Exclude blank ratings from means and report valid response counts. Do not replace missing ratings with zero.

The dining survey is a voluntary convenience sample collected during one afternoon. Students may choose whether to respond. Results describe the surveyed responses and do not establish which dining hall all students prefer.

Compare dining hall satisfaction using the mean rating and the count of non-missing ratings for each hall. A hall with a high mean but few responses has limited supporting evidence. Report missing counts separately.

Share only aggregate dining survey results. Do not publish names, student identifiers, or individual responses. An assistant must ask for approval before sending a report externally or overwriting the original data.
North, South, and East are fictional dining halls. This exercise contains synthetic data for teaching. It does not describe real campus dining operations.
The meal plan FAQ explains meal credits and guest passes. It contains no satisfaction measurements or information about how many students visit each hall.
